phrase.text: compute with numbers: between two integers they give an exact integer and, if either is real, they give a real.

runs.text: compute with numbers: between two integers they give an exact integer and, if either is real, they give a real.
to compute another value. The basic arithmetic operators are addition
, plus the minus sign in front of a number.
The type of the result depends on the operands:

blocks.description: At the top, Integer plus Integer gives Integer. Below, Integer times Real gives Real.

caption.text: Two integers give an integer; a single real is enough for the result to be real.

blocks.title: The basic sums

runs.text: Arithmetic operators only accept numbers. Adding a number and a boolean, or a number and a text, is detected before running.
Integer operations are checked in 64 signed bits: if the result does not fit, the program stops with
. There is no silent wrap-around. The minus sign applied to the smallest integer also overflows, because its opposite does not fit.

points.text: Two integers give an exact integer; if there is a real, the result is real.
Going outside the integer range stops the program.
